name: Pepperspot Peperomia
description: Peperomia prostrata 'Pepperspot' is a trailing cultivar of Peperomia prostrata in the Piperaceae family, grown for its delicate cascades of tiny round, solid green leaves on wiry reddish stems. Unlike the species form (string of turtles), Pepperspot typically lacks the strong turtle-shell vein pattern and instead looks like fine green peppercorn or coin spots along the stems. It is compact, fast-growing, and well suited to hanging baskets, shelves, and humid terrariums. Provide bright indirect light, a free-draining mix, and careful watering—allow the top of the soil to dry slightly between waterings. Non-toxic to cats and dogs. Note: trade labeling sometimes attributes this cultivar to P. rotundifolia; it is treated here as a cultivar of P. prostrata, the parent species already used in horticultural sources.
careTips: Bright indirect light; too little light causes sparse trailing growth
Allow the top 1–2 cm of soil to dry before watering; avoid soggy soil and root rot
Use a light, well-draining mix with perlite or bark
Moderate to high humidity (50–70%) suits terrariums and bathrooms
Keep temperatures around 18–27 °C; protect from cold drafts
Propagate easily from stem cuttings in soil or water
Non-toxic and safe for homes with pets
geographicOrigin: Horticultural cultivar (parent species native to Brazil)
